explanation:
The inspect confirmed the hypothesis: my candidate program reproduces both train outputs with zero mismatching cells, so I'll explain the reasoning and give the program.

## What the grids are made of

Everything sits on a background of 4. Besides stray single cells, each input contains a few small **multicolour shapes**: a body of colour 1 (or colour 2 in the test) with exactly one cell of a different "marker" colour embedded in it. For example in train pair 1 the T-shape of 1s has a 6 sitting on top of it, and the little arch of 1s has a 3 hanging below it. In train pair 2 the 3×3 ring of 1s has a 2 at its centre, the arch has a 3 inside, and the diamond has an 8 inside.

Elsewhere in the grid there are isolated single cells. Some have the same colour as a marker (the other 6 at (1,12) in pair 1, the other 3s at (12,3) and (12,14)); others, the 5s, match no shape at all.

## How the output is built

Comparing input and output:

- Every original shape disappears, and every lone 5 disappears — the output is a fresh background canvas.
- Wherever there was a lone cell of a marker colour, a copy of the shape carrying that marker appears, positioned so that **the shape's marker cell lands exactly on the lone cell**. In pair 1 the T-with-6 is reproduced at the lone 6 (1,12) → 1s at (2,11..13),(3,12); the arch-with-3 is reproduced at both lone 3s. In pair 2 the ring-with-2 is stamped at both lone 2s, the arch-with-3 at the lone 3, and the diamond-with-8 at the lone 8.
- Lone cells whose colour matches no shape (the 5s) are simply erased — they are distractors.

So the rule is a **legend / stamping** rule: each shape is a template, its minority-colour cell is the anchor, and every isolated cell of the anchor colour says "put a copy of me here".

## Checking it

I implemented exactly this — objects found with diagonal connectivity and multicolour merging (needed because in pair 2 the diamond's 1s touch only diagonally), marker = least frequent colour inside the shape, templates of size 1 are the targets — and ran it on both train pairs: 0 differing cells on each.

## Applying it to the test input

The test has three templates: a plus of 1s with a 6 centre, a diamond of four 1s with a 3 below, and a 2-coloured block with an 8 inside. The lone markers are three 6s on row 4 (x=9,12,15), one 3 at (10,10), and two 8s at (15,1) and (15,5). The output therefore has three pluses side by side on rows 2–5 (their arms touch but don't overlap), one diamond around (10,10), and two 2/8 blocks at the bottom-left. The two 5s are discarded.

## Construction stages

1. Start from a blank background canvas (all templates and stray cells erased).
2. For each template, stamp it on every lone cell of its marker colour, emitting after each template is done.
